questions.question_text: A cable-car line runs from a base station at $(1, 1)$ to a summit at $(4, 5)$, where each grid unit represents $20$ m. Find the length of the cable-car line in metres.

options.why: Added the run and rise as $3+4=7$ units before scaling, instead of using the hypotenuse of $5$.
Found the length as $5$ units but forgot to multiply by the $20$ m scale.
Found $5$ units correctly but multiplied by $100$ instead of the $20$ m scale.

questions.solution_text:
$d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$
$= \sqrt{(4 - 1)^2 + (5 - 1)^2}$
$= \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}$
$= \sqrt{25}$
$= 5 \text{ units}$
Each unit is $20$ m, so the length is $5 \times 20 = 100$ m.
